pages.text: The new ores also give early parts that need no steel.$(br2)$(l)Sheets$()$(br)A mechanical press on a depot or a belt turns one ingot into one sheet:

$(li)$(item)Lead ingot$() to $(item)lead sheet$().$(li)$(item)Nickel ingot$() to $(item)nickel sheet$().$(br2)$(l)Constantan$()$(br)In a $(item)heated$() mixer (lit blaze burner), $(item)1 copper ingot + 1 nickel ingot$() give $(item)2 constantan ingots$(). Constantan is used later for wires and electrical parts.

$(l)The cast iron chemical vat$()$(br)6 cast iron sheets, 2 lead sheets and a cast iron fluid tank make a $(item)cast iron chemical vat$(), the first vat you can build. Sulfuric acid is one of the recipes it accepts.

$(l)Waiting for steel$()$(br)$(item)Screws$() and $(item)rebar$() are not made from these metals: both come from a steel ingot in a stonecutter (4 per ingot). Keep a few early steel ingots aside for them.
The items this page talks about. Hover for details; JEI shows their recipes.
